nodes.question: What happened to the DVD that appears as the small square case near the center of the source image?
nodes.criteria: Assess the same DVD across source and edited images, using its source location and appearance to establish identity. Complete if that DVD is white in the edited image; partial if it has changed from black toward white but is not white; absent if it remains black with no requested change. Unknown if the DVD's identity or its color change cannot be established from the images. Do not count a different object or newly introduced disc as fulfillment.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The binding is truncated/ambiguous (“near (...) case near the center”) and should identify the source target precisely, then require tracking that same object into the edited image—not treating a nearby white object as evidence. The images show the small square case near the center in the source is absent in the edit; a white circular disc appears nearby, but its proximity does not establish identity or a color change. Keep the criterion’s distinction between absent progress and partial progress: partial requires visual evidence that the same target changed toward white, not merely that it disappeared while a white disc appeared. The repeated traces are valid, queried, high-confidence, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport/schema failure; their partial/no split indicates criterion application ambiguity. Clarify that disappearance or replacement without evidence of continuity is not progress, while preserving an unresolved outcome if identity/change genuinely cannot be determined. Do not infer fulfillment from the reference label alone.
